title: finding/1, ERLANG's extension
description: The erlang object of a finding/1 written by ERLANG. Fields are added as checks need them; see research/finding1-requirements.md. Every static finding carries a fix; a trace finding carries one when its statement or route is found in the source, and its counts in trace either way; a load finding carries its measurements in load.

strength.description: From the rule, as written in reference/.

client.description: The client making the call, found by where it is imported from: for no-timeout the outbound client, for n-plus-one and per-row-writes the database client.

unresolved.description: The check could not read what decides the finding (options spread from a package, a value computed at run time), so the finding is info, not a defect.

calls.description: no-timeout on an instance: how many calls on it set no timeout; each is listed in where.locations after the instance.

over.description: n-plus-one and per-row-writes: what the list the statement runs once per item of comes from: a query, request input, or a count written in the code above ten (a loop to 1,000). unknown goes with unresolved.

sequential.description: n-plus-one and per-row-writes: whether each item's statement waits for the one before (an await in the loop), rather than all starting together.

rows.description: unbounded-query: sent when the rows go into a response, loaded when every row is read to compute something, client page size when the client chooses how many rows with no cap.

connections.description: pool-sizing: the connections every deployed process can open at once (a floor when a count is unknown).

limit.description: pool-sizing: the connections the database accepts, max_connections less the reserved.

fix.description: The suggested fix (lib/fix.js). auto: edits a program can apply, re-checked by scripts/fix-test.js. guided: every place a person must change, and a note.

oneOf.description: Replace length UTF-16 code units at a 1-based line and column (columns in UTF-16 code units) of file, relative to the project root.
Make a file, which must not exist, relative to the project root.
Delete a file, which must exist, relative to the project root.

retrier.description: retry-policy: what retries, a library or a hand-written loop.

attempts.description: retry-policy: attempts per request, the first try included.

backoff.description: retry-policy: how the wait between attempts grows.

jitter.description: retry-policy: whether the wait is randomised.

table.description: missing-index: the table (or Prisma model) that needs the index.

index.description: missing-index: the columns (Prisma: fields) of the suggested index, in order.

trace.description: Trace evidence (research/trace-harness.md): counts recorded on seeded data, one request at a time. Counts are exact, so no count varies between runs. Timings (judge timing) carry the timing lock's verdict (lib/timing.js).

judge.description: statements: per request, from pg_stat_statements. rows: rows the statements returned. calls: HTTP calls per page view. bytes: a response's bytes as sent. fields: the share of a response's JSON its page never reads. pool: connections checked out of the twin's pool, during an outbound call or after the response. attempts: outbound calls the stub received for one request. hang: whether the response came while the stub never answered. repeat: statements over the same request sent several times in a row. memory: the twin's heap after a full collection, per request served. connections: connections open at the database. plans: the plan PostgreSQL chose (auto_explain). timing: milliseconds, under the timing lock.

slope.description: Extra statements or calls per extra item between the two scales; for judge memory, the heap kept per request (bytes), the least-squares slope over a soak's points.

waits.description: judge attempts: the delay the twin declared before each retry (ms), as its code asked for it (a timer), in every run; a declared value, not a measured time.

gaps.description: judge attempts, info 'wait not observed': the measured gaps between attempts (ms) in which no declared timer was seen.

r2.description: judge memory: the fit of the slope (R²); a slope counts at 0.9 or better.

ratio.description: The count at 10x over the count at 1x; null when it is infinite.

statement.description: The statement that grows, as pg_stat_statements records it.

streamed.description: The response had no Content-Length: it was streamed.

unstable.description: The two measured runs differed, so nothing is judged.

plan.description: plans: the plan node that reads the table, as auto_explain records it (Seq Scan, Index Scan, ...).

timing.description: The timing lock's verdict (lib/timing.js): reliable only with three or more samples, relative spread of 10% or less, and the one-minute load average below half the CPU count before and after.

host.description: attempts, hang: the upstream host the stub failed, as the twin addressed it.

symbol.description: hang, connections: the function, client or handler the request drove, for linking to a static finding with no endpoint.

warmup.description: Judge timing with starts (cold-start): the request each fresh process got before its routes' first requests. source: trace.json (a route the trace form adds), erlang.config.json (the app's own, configured), or fallback (a path that does not exist, answered 404: it warms the framework but not the database driver).

across.description: pool-exhaustion: the client of the other service a connection is held across.

blocking.description: blocking-work: what the synchronous call blocks on.

payload.description: oversized-payload: what makes the response or the page view too big: every column selected, no compression, or one call per item.

load.description: Load evidence (research/load-harness.md): one step of a load run at a fixed arrival rate (k6), repeated, this twin against the other. Every load finding carries the timing rule's verdict; an unreliable one is info.

step.description: The judged step's id in load.json.

samples.description: The judged quantity in each repeat.

twin.description: This twin's medians over the repeats.

other.description: The other twin's medians over the repeats.

timing.description: The timing lock's verdict (lib/timing.js): reliable only with three or more samples, relative spread of 10% or less, and the one-minute load average below half the CPU count before and after. Counts and shares with no time limit in them are exempt (exempt: true).

cooledAfterS.description: Seconds the harness waited after the step for the load average to fall below half the CPU count; null when it never did within 120 s (docs/decisions.md, Q6).

exempt.description: True for a verdict on a count, or on a share with no time limit in it (statements, calls, connections, bytes, the share of requests that failed): exempt from the timing rule, always reliable; the load averages are kept as information.

values.description: The values the message quotes (lib/values.js; docs/CONTRACT.md, measured and declared values): what this run measured, which differs between runs of the same subject, and what the code, the fixture or the judge declares, which does not. Each by the name the template gives it.

template.description: The message with each of its values replaced by {name} (a literal brace written {{ or }}): the same in every run that reaches the same verdict. The message is the template with values filled in.
